purpose: Summative artifact applying D1.1-D1.5 in one detective case. Used as Lesson 5 capstone evidence.
student_learning_goal: I can ask and answer questions about a data display and write a conclusion.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can ask and answer questions about a data display and write a conclusion.
header.character_watermark: Detective Dot and Tally together in the top-right corner with detective hats. Small (~1.5in tall combined). References both characters.

parts.student_instructions: Pick a question. Survey 5 classmates. Tally each answer.
parts.visual_layout: Top: a question line 'My question: ___'. Below: a tally chart with 3 category rows, each with a label box, tally area, and total box.

image_placeholders.description: A simple tally chart for a Grade 1 capstone worksheet, B&W line art. At the top, a labelled line 'My question: ___' for the child to write their survey question. Below: 3 category rows, each ~3.5in × 0.8in. Each row has a label box on the left, a wide tally area in the middle, and a total box on the right.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_TALLY at Part 1: instructions ask the child to survey and tally. Keywords name the visual element (tally) and activity (survey).

parts.answer_key: Any valid 5-classmate survey with consistent tally marks across 3 categories. Total tallies must equal 5.

parts.student_instructions: Use your tally to build a pictograph. Add a TITLE and LABELS.
parts.visual_layout: A blank pictograph grid (~5in × 3in) with 3 rows. Above: title line. Beside each row: label line.

image_placeholders.description: A blank pictograph grid for a Grade 1 capstone worksheet, B&W line art. ~5in × 3in with 3 empty rows. Each row has a blank label line on the left and ~6 grid cells in the middle (for one-to-one pictures). Above the grid, a thin title line. Suitable for the child to convert their tally chart into a pictograph display.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_GRID at Part 2: instructions ask the child to build a pictograph from their tally. Keywords name the format (pictograph) and required components (title, labels).

parts.answer_key: Pictograph with: a clear title (matching the question), 3 labels (matching tally categories), and pictures one-to-one matching tally counts. Total pictures = 5.

parts.student_instructions: Look at your pictograph. Write ONE sentence about what the data shows.
parts.visual_layout: A bordered rectangle (~5in × 1.5in) for writing. Above the rectangle: 'My conclusion: ___'. Inside, the child writes their conclusion sentence. Below the rectangle, a small reminder strip with sentence-frame options: 'Most children chose ___', 'The least chosen was ___'.

image_placeholders.description: A bordered rectangular writing box for a Grade 1 capstone worksheet, ~5in × 1.5in with thin solid border. Above the box: 'My conclusion: ___'. Inside, faint guide-lines for writing. Below the box, a small reminder strip listing two sentence-frame options: 'Most children chose ___' and 'The least chosen was ___'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P3_CONCLUSION at Part 3: instructions ask the child to write a conclusion sentence. Keywords name the response type (conclusion, sentence).

parts.answer_key: Any sentence that uses GROUP language (most, least, more than, fewer than) and accurately describes the pictograph. Common: 'Most children chose apples.' 'The least chosen fruit was grapes.' Strong: 'More children chose dogs than fish.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write a SECOND conclusion sentence. Use a different word (more than, fewer than).
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone — summative evidence for the unit. Score against the capstone rubric. Look for: question articulated (D1.2); tally accuracy (D1.2); pictograph with title and labels and one-to-one (D1.3); ordering implied by the conclusion language (D1.4); group-language conclusion (D1.5). Children who complete all 3 parts independently demonstrate full unit mastery.
